topic: Joyce judgment and Hoover’s testimony / destruction of minutes
claim_as_settled: Chang Yen-Mao v. Moreing (and Bewick, Moreing, and the new CEMC) opened before Mr. Justice Joyce in Chancery on January 17, 1905, and ran sixteen days. Hoover was not a named defendant (the suit was filed May 7, 1903). Under oath he “sang a new tune,” acknowledging the February 19 memorandum as binding and claiming he had tried to uphold joint management — testimony Whyte calls “disingenuous,” given his earlier letters about freeing himself of “any interference from the Chinese board” and calling that board a “farce.” On March 1, 1905, Joyce found for Chang: the memorandum was binding; the defendants’ refusal to honor it was “a flagrant breach of faith”; Joyce was appalled that Hoover “actually took possession of some of the title deeds of the property by main force”; he saw plausible grounds that nearly 425,000 shares had been defrauded; he cleared Chang, “which is more than I can say for some of the other parties concerned.” Hoover later “obtain[ed] and apparently destroy[ed] every copy of the court minutes he could find (one set has survived).”
